projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The persistent 24–27 device count combined with zero camera motion and no dog activity confirms this is a false positive from smart home devices or network noise, not actual occupancy; the household is securely at rest with no unusual activity.

The contradiction between a high, rising device count and zero camera motion or dog activity indicates the presence signal is likely inflated by stationary smart home/IoT devices rather than actual people, suggesting the home may be empty or the family is in camera-blind zones.

The sustained 18–23 connected devices paired with zero camera motion and no dog alerts on a weekday evening confirms the home is unoccupied, with the high device count attributable to smart home infrastructure (routers, TVs, consoles, security cameras) maintaining connections rather than human presence. This matters because it validates the absence state, allowing the system to safely adjust security, energy, and pet monitoring settings without false occupancy triggers.

The consistent 26–28 device count paired with zero camera motion over four hours confirms the house is likely empty and the presence metric is tracking idle IoT devices rather than occupants, which means occupancy-based automations may be triggering incorrectly.

The persistent 21–28 connected devices with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon strongly indicates the home is physically unoccupied, with the high count driven by background IoT infrastructure and personal electronics rather than active residents. This matters because it confirms a false sense of occupancy for security systems and suggests energy/water optimization is safe, though a quick verification is warranted given the children's typical afternoon schedule.

The sudden spike of 4–5 connected devices at 15:41, paired with zero camera motion, suggests new occupants (likely the children returning from school or a visitor) have connected their devices while remaining stationary or outside camera view, warranting a quick verification of entry points or a voice check.

The persistent 20-22 device count paired with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon indicates a large group of guests or remote workers likely gathered in a camera-blind area or with cameras intentionally disabled. This warrants a quick check to confirm the gathering is expected and ensure your security system is active.

The persistently high device count (19-21) combined with zero camera motion on a Thursday afternoon indicates a sustained 'home mode' (likely remote work/school), but the lack of camera activity suggests motion detection may be disabled or cameras are in a low-power state, potentially masking unexpected movement.

The consistent 19-22 device count paired with zero camera activity on a weekday morning confirms Wi-Fi presence is unreliable here; the house is likely empty or in low-occupancy mode, with the high count driven by IoT devices or network artifacts rather than people. This matters because automations relying on device count may trigger incorrectly, so motion/camera should be prioritized for occupancy detection.

The consistently high device count (21-25) paired with zero camera activity on a weekday morning suggests the network is likely dominated by stationary IoT devices rather than active human traffic, or a quiet gathering is underway. Verifying camera functionality is recommended to ensure no motion events were missed during typical morning departures.
